लिए चुने गये. इमरजेंसी के दौरान भूमिगत परचा—पोस्टर चिपकाने , बांटने का काम करने लगे. इसी आंदोलन के दौरान राजनीतिक सामग्री पढ़ने—लिखने की आदत लगी. इस आदत ने पत्रकारिता की ओर उन्मुख किया. करीब चार दशक तक सक्रिय पत्रकारिता में रहे. साहाशिये के स्वर को उभारने , बेजुबानों को आवाज देने , अनाम-गुमनाम नायकों को उभारने , उनके नायकत्व को स्थापित करना ही पत्रकारिता का मूल विषय बने , इस कोशिश में लगे रहे. उप-संपादक के रूप में 1977-1981 तक कार्यरत. 1981 में बैंक आफ इंडिया में अधिकारी के रूप में चयन हुआ. 1981 से 1984 तक बैंक आफ इंडिया की सेवा में रहे. हैदराबाद व पटना में. इसी दरम्यान भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक में भी अधिकारी के रूप में चयन हुआ. पर , मन में पत्रकारिता रच—बस चुका था. भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक के अवसर को छोड़कर और बैंक आफ इंडिया की नौकरी छोड़कर पुन: पत्रकारिता में आ गये. कोलकाता के ‘ आनंद बाजार पत्रिका ‘ समूह की मशहूर हिंदी पत्रिका ‘रविवार’ से जुड़ गये. सहायक संपादक के रूप में. 1985 से 1989 तक वहां कार्यरत रहे. 1989 में रांची से प्रकाशित होनेवाले मृतप्राय अखबार ‘ प्रभात खबर ‘ से प्रस्ताव रूप में पीएमओ से जुड़े. 1990 से जून 1991 तक. चंद्रशेखरजी के साथ वहां से इस्तीफा देकर 1991 में पुन: प्रभात खबर में वापसी. तब से जून 2016 तक , अखबार में प्रधान संपादक के रूप में कार्यरत रहे. पत्रकारिता सांस्थानिक रूप में पत्रकारिता के तीन पड़ाव बने. ‘धर्मयुग’ , ‘ रविवार’ और ‘प्रभात खबर’. पत्रकारिता के कैरियर में तीनों का अपना खास महत्व रहा. ‘धर्मयुग’ में यशस्वी संपादक धर्मवीर भारती से लेकर गणेश मंत्री जैसे पत्रकार का सान्निध्य और मार्गदर्शन मिला , जिसका गहरा असर हमेशा रहा. पत्रकारिता की वैचारिकी और सरोकार का पाठ सिखने का अवसर कैरियर के आरंभिक दिनों में ही मिला. ‘रविवार’ पत्रिका से जुड़ने के बाद बिहार , झारखंड (तब अविभाजित बिहार का ही हिस्सा) समेत देश के कई इलाकों में , ग्रासरूट रिपोर्टिंग का अवसर मिला. साथ ही संपादकीय विभाग में अहम जिम्मेवारी मिलने से नेतृत्व करने का आत्मविश्वास आया. एसपी सिंह जैसे वरिष्ठ और प्रयोगधर्मी पत्रकार के साथ काम करने का मौका मिला.पत्रकारिता के कैरियर में अहम और सबसे लंबा पड़ाव बना ‘प्रभात खबर’. सिर्फ पड़ाव ना कहकर , इसे अखबार से एकाकार हो जाने का रिश्ता कह सकते हैं. करीब 28 साल तक प्रभात खबर के साथ जुड़ाव और सफर रहा. जब ‘प्रभात खबर’ से जुड़ाव हुआ , तब यह बंदप्राय अखबार था.सरकारी दफ्तरों में भेजने के लिए प्रकाशित होनेवाला अखबार. ऐसे अखबार से जुड़ने का फैसला लेने के बाद अनेक लोगों ने मर्सियागान किया कि यह अपने पांव पर कुल्हाड़ी मारने का फैसला है. पर , मृतप्राय—बंदप्राय अखबार हिंदी की क्षेत्रीय पत्रकारिता का मॉडल अखबार बना. दस पूर्वी भारत के दस स्थानों से प्रकाशित होनेवाला अखबार ना. पत्रकारिता में हाशिये के स्वर को बुलंदी देनेवाला अखबार बना. संसाधन के अभाव के बावजूद निरंतर नवाचार और प्रयोग की वजह से हिंदी पत्रकारिता का उम्दा और नजीर अखबार बना. ‘धर्मयुग’ , ‘ रविवार’ और ‘प्रभात खबर’ से तो कैरियर के रूप में जुड़ाव रहा , पर इन तीनों से इतर अन्य जगहों पर भी लेखन चलता रहा.इनमें ‘नवभारत टाईम्स’ , ‘ दैनिक भास्कर’ , ‘ फस्टपोस्ट’ वेबसाइट , संडे (अंग्रेजी) जैसे प्रकाशन प्रमुखता से शामिल हैं.भारतीय प्रेस संस्थान की पत्रिका ‘विदुरा’ के सलाहकार संपादक रहें. पत्रकारिता के जरिये सामाजिक राजनीतिक बदलाव में सार्थक व सक्रिय हस्तक्षेप के लिए इंडिया टुडे , तहलका जैसी पत्रिका ने विशेष स्टोरी की. दिल्ली से प्रकाशित प्रतिष्ठित अंग्रेजी पत्रिका ‘सिविल सोसाइटी’ ने प्रभात खबर को भंवरजाल से निकाल हिंदी पत्रकारिता और क्षेत्रीय पत्रकारिता का एक मानक या अखिल भारतीय पत्रकारिता परिषद , कोलकाता ने महावीर प्रसाद द्विवेदी पत्रकारिता सम्मान दिया. मध्यप्रदेश की राजधानी भोपाल स्थित माधव राव सप्रे पत्रकारिता एवं शोध संस्थान ने प्रथम माधव राव सप्रे सम्मान 2008 f: Prof. Jatindra Kumar Nayak is an Indian translator, literary critic, columnist, editor, and academic from Odisha. An alumnus of Oxford University, UK, Prof. Nayak has been instrumental in bringing Odia literature to a global audience through his exemplary translations. His notable translations include Yantrarudha by Chandrasekhar Rath, rendered into English as Astride the Wheel, for which he received the 2004 Hutch Crossword Book Award for Indian Language Fiction Translation. He also won the Katha Translation Award for his English rendering of Tarun Kanti Mishra’s short story Abaroha. Prof. Nayak is the Editor-in-Chief of MargAsia, a journal dedicated to exploring the literatures and cultures of Asia and Southeast Asia. He has served as a member of the English Advisory Board of Sahitya Akademi, New Delhi, and has been a visiting professor at Ravenshaw University, IIT Bhubaneswar, and Ashoka University. Currently, he is Professor Emeritus at KISS University, Bhubaneswar, and a language expert for Odia at the New India Foundation, Bangalore.

b: Madan Mohan Danish’s simple and effortless style of poetry has afforded him a distinguished place among all. The landscape drawn by his words, which look straight into the eyes of life’s bitterness, is distinctly…
f: Madan Mohan Danish’s simple and effortless style of poetry has afforded him a distinguished place among all. The landscape drawn by his words, which look straight into the eyes of life’s bitterness, is distinctly discernable from afar. He embodies both unitary and collective sentiments of an individual in such a way that the aesthetic essence of the couplet barely lessens. He also surprises the reader with his fresh expression and new thoughts; it’s like the faint whisper of a wave gushing away the reader in its current. Death, love, life, night, etc. are his favorite motifs, intricately interwoven in couplets. His style of expression is utterly novel; it’s as if he speaks directly to his reader. In small meters, Danish has a distinct mastery, and his couplets etch deep into our memory. The fact that his poetry collection becomes sold out as soon as it’s published, testifies the wide acclaim he enjoys among his readers. In Mushairas, his name is a crowd-drawer and a stamp of success for any event. His poetry has transcended all borders and is read in several nations including, Dubai, Qatar, Sharjah, Pakistan, United States, Canada, and so on. So far, two of his books have come to light, the latest being ‘Asman Fursat Mein Hai’, which has seen a number of editions being published due to its huge demand. He has also been awarded several important literary awards, including the Madhya Pradesh Urdu Academy Award. He is currently based in Gwalior and has retired from All India Radio, Gwalior.

As a passionate advocate for literary talent, he initiated the Young Author Award 2024 to recognize emerging voices. Through his writing and publishing efforts, Subhransu Panda continues to enrich Odisha’s literary scene, offering a blend of cultural insights and contemporary themes.

b: Subroto Bagchi is Chairman of Odisha Skill Development Authority. This is a full-time assignment, in the rank of a Cabinet Minister. He was invited by Shri Naveen Patnaik, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha in 2016, to…
f: Subroto Bagchi is Chairman of Odisha Skill Development Authority. This is a full-time assignment, in the rank of a Cabinet Minister. He was invited by Shri Naveen Patnaik, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha in 2016, to set up the Odisha Skill Development Authority to harmonise the various skill initiatives of the Government. Upon taking charge, the State has a new sense of direction, instilled urgency and above all, skill development has become aspirational in the eyes of everyone. In addition to leading the Skill Development initiatives of the Government of Odisha, Subroto Bagchi has generously given his time and energy towards entrepreneurship development, attracting industrial investment into the State, leadership development in the Government, and innovation in various spheres. In March 2019, he was appointed as the Chief Spokesperson of Government of Odisha in the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. His primary role was to sensitise the people of Odisha in the dealing with the outbreak through information, education, and communication during the early days of the Pandemic. Prior to his work with the Government of Odisha, Subroto Bagchi spent four decades with the Indian IT industry where he is best known as a co-founder of Mindtree. Mindtree is one of India’s most admired software companies that built the AADHAR platform among its many other contributions. Today, Mindtree has a market cap in excess of USD 10 billion and employs 23000 people worldwide. Subroto Bagchi is a well-known writer with several business best-sellers. His books have been translated in most Indian languages as well as Chinese and Korean. He has served the boards of IIM Bengaluru, Indian Oil, IIIT Bhubaneswar and he currently serves the Board of Governors of the Software Technology Parks of India. Along with his writer wife, Susmita, Subroto Bagchi supports the cause for prevention of blindness, geriatric care, mental health, entrepreneurship development, school and vocational education with their personal resources and time. To make a small difference to their State in cancer care, they have set aside Rupees 340 crores to bring up an integrated, comprehensive, world-class, oncology platform in association with the Government of Odisha, Karunashraya and Sri Shankara Cancer Foundation. Of the Rupees 340 crores, Rupees 210 crores will be donated to Sri Shankara Cancer Foundation and Rupees 130 crores will be donated to Karunashraya for setting up their respective Units in Info-Valley, Bhubaneswar. The two centres will carry the Bagchi name. However, Susmita and Subroto Bagchi will not be institutionally connected, nor have any commercial interest whatsoever.

f: Assistant Director Suman Barsha is an acclaimed Nepali author, novelist, poet, storyteller, curator, English literature academic, artist, and social worker. She currently serves as the Assistant Director of the Kathmandu Kalinga Literary Festival (KKLF) and is actively associated with numerous national and international literary organizations, contributing to the promotion of literature, culture, and creative dialogue. A distinguished voice in contemporary Nepali literature, Suman Barsha has made significant contributions through her novels and short stories. Her writing explores a wide range of themes, including social justice, human relationships, environmental concerns, technology, science fiction, and the evolving complexities of modern society. Her narratives are known for seamlessly blending traditional storytelling with contemporary perspectives, creating thought-provoking and emotionally engaging works. Her acclaimed short story collection, Abhyantar , comprises 18 compelling stories that examine diverse subjects ranging from social issues and environmental challenges to futuristic concepts involving science fiction and robotics. The anthology reflects her literary versatility, imagination, and keen understanding of human nature. Suman Barsha is also the author of the novel Antatah Yantrana , published by Shikha Books , as well as two other novels that have further strengthened her reputation as an influential contemporary Nepali writer. Through her literary works, she continues to inspire readers with narratives that are both intellectually stimulating and socially relevant. Beyond her literary achievements, Suman Barsha is recognized for her dedication to promoting literature, nurturing emerging writers, and engaging in cultural and social initiatives. Her multifaceted contributions as a writer, educator, curator, artist, and social worker have established her as a respected figure in Nepal’s literary and cultural landscape.

b: Sushil Doshi is an Indian sports commentator, journalist, and writer, widely recognized as the pioneer of Hindi-language cricket commentary in the country, having begun his career with All India Radio in 1968 during a…
f: Sushil Doshi is an Indian sports commentator, journalist, and writer, widely recognized as the pioneer of Hindi-language cricket commentary in the country, having begun his career with All India Radio in 1968 during a Ranji Trophy match. Born in 1947 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, he graduated in engineering from Shri Govindram Seksaria Institute of Technology and Science while nurturing an interest in Hindi literature, which shaped his distinctive commentary style emphasizing grammatical accuracy and vivid descriptions. Over a career spanning more than five decades, Doshi has provided commentary for over 400 One Day Internationals, 85 Test matches, and ten Cricket World Cups, making him the only Hindi commentator to cover that many global events. His work extended from radio to television on Doordarshan, where he popularized cricket among Hindi-speaking audiences, particularly in rural India, through phrases like his famous 1979 warning during an India-England Test at The Oval: “Jin logon ko dil ki bimari hai, woh commentary na sune…” (Those with heart conditions should not listen to the commentary). In recognition of his contributions to sports commentary in Hindi, he received the Padma Shri, India’s fourth-highest civilian award, in 2016 from President Pranab Mukherjee. Doshi’s influence extends beyond broadcasting; a dedicated commentary box at Holkar Cricket Stadium in Indore bears his name, and he served on the All India Council for Sports (2020–2023), an advisory body under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, advocating for indigenous games, differently-abled participation, and private sector investment in sports. As of 2025, he remains active, critiquing modern commentary for its use of slang and urging practitioners to prioritize considerate, proper language to preserve the medium’s reach and integrity.

f: Ms Swati Pandey, Vice Chairman & Managing Director of Maharashtra Airport Development Company, is a distinguished career bureaucrat with over 28 years of leadership in aviation, infrastructure development, public policy, financial inclusion, and atomic energy. As Postmaster General of Mumbai, she helmed one of India Post’s most dynamic regions and earned international academic recognition for Project Kamathipura, a Harvard-published case study on socio-financial inclusion in one of India’s most marginalized communities. Her debut book, “Invisible in Plain Sight”, is a powerful examination of the lives of the sex workers of Kamathipura pushed to society’s edges-an unflinching exploration built on empathy, rigorous research, and a deep commitment to truth. Through this work, she compels readers to confront entrenched biases and re-examine notions of privilege, dignity, and visibility. She is also credited with initiating the renovation of the 115-year-old Mumbai General Post Office through deep research on its unique Indo-Saracenic architectural style. Beyond governance, Ms. Pandey is a National Award-winning filmmaker for “Elephants Do Remember” and an evocative storyteller. A Ted-x speaker and ISB alumna, she continues to inspire through her rare blend of administrative acumen, creative depth, and unwavering dedication to social equity and cultural preservation.

b: Tanaya Patnaik Executive Director, Sambad Group Tanaya Patnaik is Executive Director of the Sambad Group and heads the radio, television and digital wings of the media house. She is an alumnus of the prestigious Warwick…
f: Tanaya Patnaik Executive Director, Sambad Group Tanaya Patnaik is Executive Director of the Sambad Group and heads the radio, television and digital wings of the media house. She is an alumnus of the prestigious Warwick Business School in London. She is instrumental in giving conventional media, a new and enhanced digital look and heads three leading news web portals (www.sambad.in, www.kanaknews.com and www.sambadenglish.com ) in the state with an unparalleled social media presence. Tanaya Patnaik, who leads the print, radio, television, and digital divisions at Odisha’s leading media house, Sambad Group, is passionate about new media and has been a driving force behind the group’s digital expansion. As a proud Odia, she actively promotes Odia culture through Sambad’s platforms. In 2014, Tanaya introduced the ‘Street Store’ concept to India, a rent-free, pop-up clothing store for the underprivileged. She also spearheaded the ‘Sambad 100 Women Edit-a-thon,’ which focused on creating and editing Wikipedia entries for notable Odia women, and organized ‘UNZIP,’ an open mic event for women to celebrate International Women’s Day with innovative, women-centric activities. Her monologue series, ‘Pause with Tanaya Patnaik,’ addresses contemporary issues and highlights Odia tradition and culture. Additionally, she founded Choklate Productions, which produced the acclaimed historical play “Ahe Nilashaila.” This play has been staged in Bhubaneswar, New Delhi, Bengaluru, and Pilgrim Town Puri, coinciding with the inauguration of the Jagannath Temple Heritage Corridor project.

Prior to his active involvement in politics, Tuhin had been among the most prolific Indian writers with a knack for experimenting with unorthodox genres. Tuhin’s book, Modi’s Northeast Story, is a rare anthology of 23 essays that document the transformation of India’s northeastern states under PM Modi. His books have traversed a wide range of subjects across both fiction and nonfiction genres. His recent book Climate Action India documents India’s initiatives towards attaining the ambitious NET Zero carbon emissions target set by PM Narendra Modi. Tuhin has authored 14 books to date. Currently, as a popular media voice of the BJP, Tuhin has been vocal and articulate on all recent political issues in his articles and on TV news debates. He also has to his credit over 300 articles written in various media outlets.

f: उर्मिला शिरीष हिंदी साहित्य जगत में एक मजबूत हस्ताक्षर मानी जाती हैं। इनका जन्म 19 अप्रैल 1959 को मध्यप्रदेश दतिया जिले में एक सभ्रांत, प्रतिष्ठित और उच्च शिक्षित परिवार में हुआ। पिता डॉ. डी.पी. गोस्वामी उद्योगपति थे एवं माता श्रीमती गिरिजा देवी गोस्वामी एक सरल सहज घरेलू महिला हैं। उर्मिला जी की प्रारंभिक शिक्षा गाँव में हुई। पुनः मिडिल तक की शिक्षा डबरा में हुई। उन्होंने हायर सेकेण्डरी की परीक्षा मा. विद्यालय दतिया से प्रथम श्रेणी में पास की। अपनी मेधा का परिचय देते हुए उन्होंने स्नातक प्रथम श्रेणी से एवं स्नातकोत्तर की परीक्षा में प्रवीण्य सूची में तृतीय स्थान प्राप्त किया। गुरुनानकदेव विश्वविद्यालय, अमृतसर से ‘मोहन राकेश के कथा साहित्य में नारी पात्रों का अध्ययन’ विषय पर पीएचडी की उपाधि प्राप्त की। 2010 में ‘गोविन्द मिश्र के कथा साहित्य में भारतीयता की अवधारणा’ विषय पर डी.लिट् की उपाधि प्राप्त की।

b: Vikas Swarup, (IFS Rtd), Diplomat, Author Vikas Swarup, born on June 22, 1961, is a retired Indian diplomat and acclaimed writer. He concluded his distinguished career in the Indian Foreign Service as Secretary (West)…
f: Vikas Swarup, (IFS Rtd), Diplomat, Author Vikas Swarup, born on June 22, 1961, is a retired Indian diplomat and acclaimed writer. He concluded his distinguished career in the Indian Foreign Service as Secretary (West) at the Ministry of External Affairs on June 30, 2021. During his tenure, he served as the High Commissioner of India to Canada and as the official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs. Swarup’s diplomatic career, which began in 1986, saw him serve in various capacities across Indian missions in Turkey, the United States, Ethiopia, the United Kingdom, South Africa, and Japan. Swarup is best known as the author of the novel Q & A, which was adapted into the Oscar-winning film Slumdog Millionaire. The novel, an international bestseller, has been translated into 43 languages and received several prestigious awards. His other notable works include Six Suspects and The Accidental Apprentice. Swarup has also written for prominent publications such as TIME, Newsweek, and The Guardian, and has participated in major literary festivals around the world. Known for his motivational talks, Swarup continues to engage audiences globally with his insights on literature and diplomacy.

f: Yatindra Mishra, a celebrated poet and literary connoisseur, has enriched the world of Indian literature with his profound poetry, thoughtful translations, and exceptional editing. His works capture the essence of Indian aesthetics, blending the classical with the contemporary in a style that is both evocative and timeless. An accomplished author, Mishra has penned several acclaimed books, including Sur Ki Baradari and Akhtari: The Life and Music of Begum Akhtar, a definitive biography of the legendary ghazal queen. His ability to portray the nuanced interplay between music, literature, and culture has won him widespread admiration. As a recipient of prestigious awards like the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Raza Foundation Award, Yatindra Mishra’s literary contributions have been celebrated both nationally and internationally. His translations and essays bridge linguistic and cultural gaps, making Indian literature accessible and relatable to a global audience. Mishra’s mastery lies not only in his poetry but also in his ability to illuminate the lives of iconic figures from Indian art and music. His work reflects a deep understanding of India’s cultural heritage, resonating with readers across generations.

His contributions to Hindi poetry are celebrated for their authenticity, honesty, and ability to resonate universally.
